title_as_printed: Table 1. 25C methane solubilities in single-salt solutions, distilled water and seawater
pressure_note: psia; system pressure of the methane headspace set by gas input/output, read on a Heise gauge (dead-weight accuracy 1 psia); total pressure (gas phase is methane + water vapour; no partial-pressure correction stated)
layout: wide: one row per solution, one CH4-molality column per pressure

composition.other_species: Na2CO3, K2CO3, NaHCO3, KHCO3, K2SO4 (outside the six-ion set); seawater 34.84 permil (row from the authors' earlier paper)

conversion_needs: Seawater row: salinity 34.84 permil, data from Stoessell and Byrne (1982), footnote **
Salt molality header carries footnote * 'Unless otherwise indicated' (the seawater row is in permil)
notes: The builder must melt the three pressure columns into three rows per solution (P = 350, 550, 750 psia). Label rows set the salt name for the following molality rows (path composition.per_row_salt). 'Distilled' and 'water' are printed on two lines with the data on the 'water' line; written as label row 'Distilled water' plus one data row with empty Salt Molality. CH4 molalities were obtained from molar values using solution densities interpolated from 20 C densities (Weast); not corrected for dissolved-gas volume (< 0.0001 molal). Distilled-water values are averages of several measurements. Bicarbonate solutions needed CO2 corrections (CO2 5-50 % of flashed gas), lowering accuracy. 2026-10-11 coordinator: the wide table (one value column per pressure) is mapped by three mappings over the same CSV (key csv), one per printed pressure; the original wide mapping is kept as mapping_1_wide_original.json.txt.
